How much does a car wrap cost in Toronto? (2026)

Published starting prices from our own estimator, what moves the number up or down, and how to compare quotes from different GTA shops.

By the Satin Graphic teamUpdated October 10, 2026
On this pageThe short answerWhat changes the priceColour change vs printed commercial wrapWhy quotes vary between shopsRelated costsHow to get an exact priceQuestionsRelatedWrap cost estimatorColour change wrapsCommercial wraps

The short answer

At our shop in Vaughan, a full wrap starts at about $2,800 for a car, $3,400 for an SUV and $3,200 for a pickup truck, before 13% HST. Commercial vans start at $3,950 (Transit-size), and box trucks at $5,800. These are the same starting prices our online estimator uses for customers anywhere in Toronto and the GTA.

VehicleFull wrap from
Car$2,800
SUV$3,400
Pickup Truck$3,200
Minivan$3,600
Transit Van$3,950
Sprinter Van$4,300
Box Truck$5,800
Trailer$4,800
Bus$8,500

Partial coverage costs less: in our estimator, decals and lettering run about 22% of the full-wrap price, a partial wrap about 45% and a ¾ wrap about 70%.

What changes the price

  • Vehicle size. A compact car takes far less film and labour than a full-size SUV. Our estimator adds about 8% for mid-size and 16% for full-size bodies.
  • Coverage. Lettering, partial, ¾ or full — see the percentages above.
  • Finish. Matte and satin films cost about 12% more than gloss in our estimator; chrome and colour-shift films cost more again.
  • Roof. Adding the roof adds about 12%.
  • Design. If you need a printed commercial design, our design service is $250 + tax. Colour changes need no design.
  • Complexity and condition. Deep bumpers, spoilers, door jambs and lots of trim removal add labour. Paint must be factory or a fully cured professional repaint — peeling clear coat can’t be wrapped.

Colour change vs printed commercial wrap

A colour change uses solid-colour cast film such as 3M 2080 or Avery SW900 — gloss, satin, matte, chrome or colour-flip — and needs no design. A printed commercial wrap is printed in-house on cast wrap film (3M IJ180 or Avery MPI 1105) and sealed under a laminate, and it needs a layout built on your vehicle’s template. The starting prices above apply to both; the final number depends on the film and coverage. See colour change wraps and commercial wraps.

Why quotes vary between shops

  • Film type. Cast film conforms to curves and lasts longer than cheaper calendered film. Ask which film and laminate are being quoted.
  • Disassembly. Removing handles, lights and trim so the film tucks behind edges takes longer than cutting on the panel, but it looks better and lifts less.
  • Workmanship warranty. We give 5 years against lifting and peeling; compare what each shop offers in writing.
  • Install environment. A clean, climate-controlled bay matters, especially in an Ontario winter.

Related costs

  • Paint protection film: partial front $900–$1,400, full front $1,800–$2,600, full body $5,500–$7,500 (gloss). See PPF.
  • Window tint: sides and back glass on a sedan from about $249 (standard) or $448 (ceramic). See window tint.
  • Vehicle lettering: about 22% of a full wrap — see vehicle lettering.

How to get an exact price

Use the estimator for a ballpark in under a minute, then send us the year, make and model, a photo and (for commercial wraps) your logo. We’ll confirm the film and a firm price. Prices on our site are in Canadian dollars and before HST.

Questions

Is a wrap cheaper than paint?
Often, yes — especially compared with a quality full respray that includes door jambs. A wrap is also reversible and protects the factory paint. See our wrap vs paint guide for the full comparison.
Does the price include HST?
No. Prices on our site are in CAD before 13% HST.
How much is a wrap for a Tesla Model 3 or Model Y?
Use the car (sedan) or SUV starting price as a guide — $2,800 and $3,400 — then the estimator adjusts for size, finish and roof. We template EV camera cut-outs and panel gaps to factory spec.
Do you need a deposit?
Online estimates in our shop use a 50% deposit to book the work; we confirm the deposit with your final quote.

Written by the Satin Graphic team at our shop in Vaughan, Ontario. Prices are in CAD before HST and come from our published estimator; we update this guide when they change. Questions? Contact us or call (905) 962-6222.
